Mr. Nawaf bin Saeed Ahmad Al-Malkiy, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to Pakistan @AmbassadorNawaf, called on the Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister, Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50. They exchanged views on the latest regional developments and underscored the need to strengthen collective efforts aimed at promoting dialogue and diplomacy. They reaffirmed their commitment to further deepening Pakistan-Saudi Arabia relations across all areas of mutual interest for the benefit of both nations.

Lord Aamer Sarfraz called on Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50. Lord Sarfraz appreciated the Deputy Prime Minister’s continued and proactive role in advancing regional peace and stability. He also briefed the DPM/FM on matters concerning the Pakistani diaspora in the United Kingdom, including key issues faced by the community and their valuable contributions to both countries. They also exchanged views on the evolving political landscape in the UK. The Deputy Prime Minister underscored the importance of further strengthening Pakistan-UK bilateral relations. He highlighted that the Pakistani diaspora, including distinguished parliamentarians like Lord Sarfraz, serves as a vital bridge between Pakistan and the UK. DPM/FM expressed confidence that members of the diaspora will continue to play a constructive role in deepening people-to-people ties, trade, and investment between the two countries.

Deeply saddened by the passing away of His Highness Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, the Former Amir of the State of Qatar. The Father Amir, late Sheikh Hamad was a great leader and statesman whose wisdom, foresight and dedication to public service, transformed Qatar into a modern, prosperous and globally respected nation. His enduring contributions to the welfare of his nation and its people, as well as to regional peace, development and international cooperation, will be remembered for generations to come. On behalf of the people and the Government of Pakistan, as well as on my own behalf, I extend our heartfelt condolences to my Dear Brother the Amir of Qatar His Highness Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, the distinguished members of the Al Thani family, the Government, as well as the brotherly people of Qatar on this solemn occasion. We stand in solidarity with them in this moment of profound grief. We will always cherish the Father Amir’s warmth, kindness and deep affection for Pakistan, as well as the fond memories of his many visits to our country. May Allah Almighty grant the departed Father Amir, the highest place in Jannat ul Firdaus, and May He shower His blessings upon the Royal Family and our Qatari brothers and sisters to bear this irreparable loss with strength, patience and fortitude. Ameen.

Shot entirely in the Chaoshan dialect, the film draws its narrative core from "qiaopi," letters and remittances sent home by overseas Chinese. The feature delicately depicts the bittersweet perseverance of early overseas Chinese, who upheld integrity, familial duty and unwavering hometown affection while striving to build lives abroad. It has become one of China's most unexpected box-office successes this year. (Source: Xinhua)

If social media posts of Judge Hamayoun Dilawar are authentic (Tosha Khana Case Judge), this is alarming and raises serious and reasonable doubts on credibility of trial being conducted by him. In my view, propriety demands that he should immediately recuse or disassociate himself from the case. It needs to be noted that Seven Member Bench of the Supreme Court of Pakistan in Malik Qayyum Case (reported in 2001 PLD SC 568) held that bias on part of the judge vitiates judicial proceedings. The court further held that an accused has a right of a fair trial by a judicial minded person, not by someone functioning under an influence or bias as the same paralyses his judicial faculties to conduct fair trial. Bias would vitiate judicial proceedings if such circumstances exist. Bias robs the judge of the confidence that a litigant may have in the judge. Court further held that bias is mental disposition or attitude towards a particular person and covers all kind of hostilities and prejudices against him.

Trump Accounts are no longer going to be optional- so if you ever plan on having a child in the USA, you should read what I found: According to the @SocialSecurity Administration's announcement last week, they are modifying the hospital birth registration form so that a Trump Account is AUTOMATICALLY created for your child through that same process. It will be bundled into the Enumeration at Birth program (EAB), which is the already automated gov pipeline that gives your newborn a Social Security number. It’s one box that you check, you don’t have the option of unbundling it. So if you want your kid to have a Social Security number, they have to have a Trump account. Which is strange, because according to the IRS and @USTreasury’s public announcements, these accounts only open when a parent actively elects to open one. So which is it? Why is nobody in the government interested in explaining this flagrant contradiction? Who is going to answer the basic question of what a parent does if they don’t want a government-linked investment account (one that collects biometric data, by the way) created for their child at the exact moment their child’s Social Security number issued? They can call it a savings account all they want, but a $1,000 deposit is a hell of a cheap price for building a lifelong financial file on every American child before they can consent to anything. And once the government normalizes linking a person’s identity, financial activity, and predictive systems from birth, who gets to decide what that data will be used to predict later? We deserve answers immediately. @ndstudio @WhiteHouse

Luton, UK: Shaykh-ul-Islam Dr Muhammad Tahir-ul-Qadri Delivers Keynote Address at "Shan-e-Ahl-e-Bait-e-Nabvi ﷺ Conference" His Eminence Shaykh-ul-Islam Dr Muhammad Tahir-ul-Qadri, founding leader of Minhaj-ul-Quran International, delivered the keynote address at the "Shan-e-Ahl-e-Bait-e-Nabviﷺ Conference", organised on the occasion of the "Ta'ziyati Reference of Pir Syed Abdul Qadir Shah Jillani (R.A)" under the auspices of Markazi Jama'at-e-Ahle Sunnat (UK & Overseas) at Jamia Islamia Ghousia Trust, Luton. Addressing a large gathering of scholars, community leaders and students of knowledge, Shaykh-ul-Islam delivered a profound Qur’anic exposition of Ayat al-Tatheer (The Verse of Purification) from Surah al-Ahzab (33:33): اِنَّمَا یُرِیْدُ اللهُ لِیُذْهِبَ عَنْکُمُ الرِّجْسَ اَهْلَ الْبَیْتِ وَیُطَہِّرَکُمْ تَطْہِیْرًا “Stay in your homes and do not display your charm, like the displaying of the former (days of) ignorance. Establish the prayer, pay the alms due and keep obeying Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ). Indeed, Allah only desires to keep all (forms and causes of) impurity away from you, O Members of the (Prophet’s) Family, and purify you with a thorough purifying.” Shaykh-ul-Islam explained that this blessed verse is a clear and unequivocal declaration of the unique rank, spiritual excellence and divinely bestowed purity of the blessed Ahl al-Bayt (ʿalayhim al-salām). He stated that Almighty Allah Himself has declared His exclusive will to remove every form of rijs—including every impurity, spiritual defect, doubt, moral corruption and anything contrary to goodness—and to grant them complete and perfect taṭhīr. Explaining the Qur’anic language, Shaykh-ul-Islam emphasised that the verse is not merely a command for the Ahl al-Bayt to attain purity through their own efforts. Rather, it is a decisive declaration that Allah ﷻ Himself undertook their complete purification. This divine act establishes their honour, purity and spiritual rank through the Qur’an itself. He further explained that the emphatic expression “وَيُطَهِّرَكُمْ تَطْهِيرًا” signifies not an ordinary form of purification but a complete, perfect and divinely bestowed purification encompassing every aspect of their belief, intentions, character, conduct, sacrifice and spiritual excellence. He stressed that the sacrifices of the Ahl al-Bayt, particularly the events of Karbala, must be understood through this Qur’anic declaration rather than through political or worldly interpretations. Elaborating on the unparalleled virtues and elevated status of the Ahl al-Bayt in the light of the Holy Qur’an and authentic Prophetic traditions, Shaykh-ul-Islam affirmed that love, reverence and loyalty to the Ahl al-Bayt are fundamental to the creed of Ahl al-Sunnah. He urged believers to return to the Qur’an and Sunnah when understanding their status and warned against allowing polemics or distorted historical narratives to shape their perception. He described the blessed Household of the Holy Prophet ﷺ as the purest embodiment of his guidance, character and spiritual legacy, whose lives continue to illuminate the path of faith, knowledge, piety and moral excellence. The conference was attended by Pir Syed Mazhar Hussain Gillani, President of Markazi Jama’at-e-Ahle Sunnat (UK & Overseas); Pir Syed Munawar Hussain Shah Jamati; Syed Ali Abbas Bukhari, President of Minhaj-ul-Quran International UK; Allama Qazi Abdul Aziz Chishti MBE, Secretary General of Markazi Jama’at-e-Ahle Sunnat (UK & Overseas); alongside distinguished scholars, community leaders and members of the Muslim community from across the United Kingdom. The gathering concluded with collective prayers for the unity of the Muslim Ummah and for peace, stability and prosperity throughout the world. #AhlulBayt #ProphetMuhammad #ShaykhUlIslam #DrTahirulQadri #Luton #IslamicEvent #UKMuslims #MarkaziJamaatEAhleSunnat #LoveForAhlulBayt #MQIUK

Africa’s future will be shaped in its rural economies and areas. Today at @IFAD, I was pleased to co-host with Italy the event “Advancing the Italian Mattei Plan: Scaling Joint Investments in Agriculture and Food Systems.” The #MatteiPlan reflects an important shift in international cooperation with Africa: moving from traditional donor-recipient models towards equal-to-equal partnership, shared ownership, co-investment and mutual benefit. The third annual progress report to the Italian Parliament shows how this approach is moving from vision to implementation across priority areas including agriculture, water, energy, infrastructure, education and health, with IFAD recognized among the international partners supporting this agenda. This direction is closely aligned with IFAD’s mandate. We invest with governments and rural communities to strengthen smallholder agriculture, build resilient value chains, expand access to finance and markets, and create opportunities where they are needed most. Italy and IFAD’s collaboration under the Mattei Plan is now moving from alignment to implementation: Côte d’Ivoire is partnering with Italy and IFAD to advance a major milestone through the Agro-Industrial Pole Project in the North-East. Italy’s €100 million co-financing will complement IFAD’s US$75 million investment to support climate-adaptive agriculture, strengthen value chains and improve food and nutrition security for more than 35,000 rural families, around 220,000 people. The Government of Senegal is working with Italy, IFAD, @TheOPECFund and @EIB on a US$265 million co-investment programme to support food sovereignty and reach more than one million people. With Angola, we are exploring further collaboration in the coffee value chain, drawing on Italian expertise and private sector engagement. These examples show how public investment, technical expertise and private sector partnerships can come together to deliver lasting impact at the first mile of food systems. With more than 60 per cent of IFAD’s portfolio in Africa, and with our country presence, IFAD is a strong partner of the Mattei Plan. As we look towards #IFAD14, with its focus on market integration, employment and resilience, this partnership offers a strong operational platform to scale joint investments with African countries. My thanks to the Government of Italy, Ambassadors from our African Member States, institutional partners and private sector actors for today’s important discussion and for their shared commitment to investing in rural prosperity. @ItalyMFA_int | @GruppoCDP | @Palazzo_Chigi | @SocialMasaf | @MEF_GOV

For those familiar with the Left, what happened to Karim Khan, Graham Platner and Cesar Chavez is straight out of the playbook of the purges: "bourgeois immorality". Here's how revolutionary discipline works. While people were were always purged for political reasons, the public charge to make it odious was nearly always personal "decadence". For example Genrik Yagoda reported to Stalin about "pederast activists" involved in orgies and alleged espionage/counter-revolutionary activities. This is how he strung people up. Then he himself was arrested and executed with raids on his apartments and dacha uncovering a large collection of pornographic materials. He died begging for his life from Yezhov his successor. Yezhov (AKA "the dwarf") was later arrested and executed by Beria, for among other crimes organizing drunken sexual orgies in his Kremlin apartment, involving both male and female partners and engaging in the most perverted forms of debauchery. He too died pleading for mercy but none was given. When he fell Beria himself was accused of kidnapping hundreds of young girls and raping them in a special soundproofed room. These acts were framed as "bourgeois immorality," sexual deviancy, and moral corruption — the same rhetorical category used against Yagoda and Yezhov. He met the same end as his predecessors. The big mystery of the Communist Party is how it can be so strictly morally revolutionary and yet so full of perverts at the same time. How could an organization so skilled at parsing pronouns, quick to take umbrage at the slightest disrespect and of such ethical standards be so full of scumbags? The obvious answer is it 's all a sham. The whole damn edifice is rotten and it's held together by reciprocal blackmail with each holding the goods on others. Just imagine the ICC sitting in judgment of creeps when it turns out to have been led by a creep all along.

Pamięć trwa, buduje naszą przyszłość i musi zwyciężać na naszych oczach. Dlatego nie chcemy i nie zgodzimy się na obecność w Polsce czerwono-czarnej flagi, pod którą zamknęła się ideologia ukraińskiego nacjonalizmu, odpowiedzialna za mordowanie polskich kobiet i dzieci oraz całych rodzin, skazując ojców na patrzenie na śmierć synów, a matki na śmierć córek. Survivability in Context: The A-10 in Operation DESERT STORM “I haven’t had a day off since the shooting started. I have, as of [February 10], dropped 17 tons of Mk-82, 6 tons of Rockeye anti-tank CBU; fired 14 Maverick missiles, and shot 3.400 rounds of 30mm party mix at various tanks, APC’s, and artillery sites in Iraq and Kuwait. The A-10 is doing things no one ever anticipated, including deep strike/interdiction on mobile Scud launchers, Wild Weasel duty, armed recce, escort, air-to-air, cargo (mail delivery) and of course, SAR. I’ll be honest—70-80 miles behind enemy lines is no place for the Hog, but so far we’ve done o.k. They tell me this builds character. We can’t wait for the ground war to start so we can begin doing Close Air Support.” --anonymous A-10 Pilot, Operation DESERT STORM “I take back every bad thing I ever said about the A-10; I love ‘em—they’re saving our asses!” --Gen Charles “Chuck” Horner, Combined Forces Air Component Commander Depending on who’s writing the article, the A-10’s service record in Operation DESERT STORM is either immediately maligned or heralded. In response to the numerous detractors, I offer this in-depth and researched rebuttal to the claims that the Hog’s performance in 1991 proves its irrelevance in all major combat operations. The quotations that open this discussion showcase the dichotomy of the situation. An author opining about the vulnerability or inappropriateness in the inventory seizes upon the opinion of the A-10 operating 70-80 miles behind the front. Indeed, the casualties that the Hog community took over the Republican Guard during this timeframe seem to support that contention, and represent the bulk of arguments against the A-10. Many pundits point out that the A-10s were “pulled back” after suffering catastrophic losses. As always, a great deal of context must be applied to the historical record. That context BEST comes from the compiled stories of the Hog Drivers themselves, which William Smallwood detailed exhaustingly in his work, “Warthog: Flying the A-10 in the Gulf War.” As one carefully looks into this context, the line from our opening quotation begins to shine as perhaps the most relevant: “The A-10 is doing things no one ever anticipated…” The question that a discerning disciple asks comes as “WHY were A-10s tasked to operate 70-80 miles behind enemy lines against the most potent units of the Iraqi military? In short-form, because no one else could get the job done. That’s a knife-hand throat-punch that some might immediately dismiss as 30mm chest-thumping or peacocking. So let’s dive into the historical record and support the contention. A-10s started losing aircraft in DS when they were tasked to do something beyond what they should have. Before the ground offensive launched, General Schwartzkopf needed 50% attrition of Iraqi units, especially those of the Republican Guard. Aircraft with the best sensors were providing inconclusive BDA, and General Horner knew that there was one community that he could rely on to get the answers; You guessed it, the A-10s. With nothing more than eyeballs and binoculars, they went up there and got the numbers... and lost a few of their own in doing so. Additionally, answering non-standard tasking, they were asked to set oil trenches ablaze, and that ended poorly, losing an A-10 after multiple passes attempting something in combat that equated to “making it up on the spot.” One A-10 pilot sacrificed himself by continuing to fight in the target area where his wingman was just shot down-- Steve Phyllis gave his life trying to protect his wingman- the only thing that could keep him from fighting for his brother, was his own death. Also of extreme note, A-10s successfully accomplished direct attacks on SA-3s and SA-6 missile systems—again, because they were called up based both on their successes and the inabilities of other communities to get the job done! These events contributed to the labeling of the Hog as the RF-OA-10G during the war. William Smallwood illustrates the lead-up to this raid in the following passage: “We were specifically tasked against an SA-3 site, but we learned later at the intel briefing that we were going to be near four SA-8s and two Rolands at Ali Al Salem, that we were going to be inside an SA-2 ring and kissing the edge of an SA-6 ring—plus being vulnerable to all the AAA they had in the area.” The mission was successful, and “it just encouraged the guys in Riyadh to say, ‘Hey, guys, go on up north in Kuwait and strike those SA-6s.’” Smallwood writes, “That is what they did, of course.” NO A-10s were lost in those raids. Nearly all hits were attributed to infrared missiles that were better able to acquire and engage the A-10s because they were still painted green and easier to see in the daytime, a limitation that USAF brass had been briefed upon prior to the war. "Bring 'em green or don't bring 'em” was what the community was allegedly told. Of the losses in Desert Storm, two A-10s flew as single ship without mutual support, and most occurred after a minimum of five passes in the same target area. In an article for the Project on Government Oversight (POGO), Pierre Sprey and Winslow Wheeler write: “In a 235 page unclassified report, GAO extensively assessed the Desert Storm Air War. That report evaluated the aircraft survivability data in some detail. The casualty figures cited above are indeed accurate, but GAO also found that the stealthy F-117 flew so few combat sorties and the A-10s flew so many that their survival rates were statistically indistinguishable: GAO found that "This calculation showed that 0 hits would be the most likely outcome for a non-stealthy aircraft [including the A-10] conducting 1,788 strikes [the number of missions performed by the F-117]. This indicates that although there were no F-117 casualties in Desert Storm, the difference between its survivability and other aircraft may arise from its smaller number of strikes as much as other factors." GAO also found the total casualty rate of the A-10 (for aircraft both shot down and damaged) was extremely low, just 0.0023 aircraft per sortie, and that it was zero for the missions the A-10 flew at night-the only environment the F-117 operated in. Significantly, the A-10 flew sorties more frequently at night than did the F-117, and it faced both daytime and nighttime defenses more lethal than the type deployed around "downtown Baghdad" that the F-117 typically flew against, according to GAO. Both the A-10 and the F-117 also flew in the Kosovo Air War in 1999 against Serbia. In that conflict, one F-117 was shot down, and one was significantly damaged. Flying a greater number of sorties, no A-10 was shot down. --POGO.org, “Chuck Hagel’s A-10 Legacy” Pierre Sprey and Winslow Wheeler pogo.org/analysis/2014/02/ch… A similar discussion on actual A-10 casualties can be found on John Q. Public’s site: jqpublicblog.com/csaf-misrep… The key takeaway from this initial discussion balances two points: first, the A-10 as a weapon system was CRITICAL during the execution of Operation DESERT STORM: the 144 A-10s deployed represented about 17 and 30% of the total sorties (depending on source and data) but accounted for MORE THAN 50% of the total damage inflicted on the Iraqi military. The A-10s and their Hog Drivers were asked to do nearly impossible things, and they got it done. They took some significant hits, lost some friends, but most importantly: THEY DID WHAT THEY WERE ASKED TO DO AND WERE SUCCESSFUL IN ACCOMPLISHING THE TASKS GIVEN TO THEM. That fact CANNOT be overstated, and returns the discussion to the quotation by General Horner. A reputed critic of the A-10, he bellowed that now infamous quotation in the heat of battle as the venerable Warthog answered his challenge and “saved [their] asses.” Later, he would return to the ceaseless criticism of the platform, but when the cards were down, he admitted what the A-10 community already knew. They’d do the job that was asked of them, no matter the cost. Fast-forward 22 years: A-10s were assigned to a very risky mission of escorting C-130s and C-17s conducting the airborne assault on Saddam International airport. The Hogs were assigned the task of trolling the route for air defenses, and the threat level was deemed so high that planners expected to lose 25% of the airlifters, and up to 50% of the A-10s. The kicker is that the Hogs would fly the mission TWICE—once the night before to begin finding, fixing, and eliminating the defenses, so pilots assigned to this mission were accepting a 25% chance of survival (according to the planners). Not a single one flinched or asked to be removed from the mission. The mission was never flown as ground forces overran the airport more quickly than originally envisioned. Every pilot assigned to that mission may have been anxious, but their first thoughts were for the airlifters and paratroopers aboard those heavies—each loss there would claim between fifty and seventy-five Americans, and the A-10 pilots took the responsibility of escorting that formation with the utmost seriousness. We can journey further into the details of this rabbit hole and prove that the A-10 is far more survivable than acknowledged, and when compared to all other fighters as a class comparison, it more than holds its own. In conducting research on EVERY A-10 casualty, the numbers actually support the viability of the Hog, not the other way around. 1991. 13 "fast-movers" were shot down before the first A-10 got bagged. 13. Including 2x F-15Es and 2x F-16s. Also in that list were the F/A-18, A6E, AC-130, OV-10, F-14, AV-8 and F-4. Admittedly, context matters-- target location... threat environment... package composition... etc. However, as mentioned earlier, A-10s were tasked specifically against Surface to Air Missile sites themselves, and executed those missions without casualties. 4 A-10s were shot down, 2 of which were single ship with no visual mutual support and had spent extensive time over the same target area. One loss was an aircraft that executed a belly landing after FIVE passes attacking oil trenches and trying to light them on fire, and another was lost on an attempted landing with significant battle damage. Interestingly: If A-10s only ever accomplished one attack and then returned to base, the loss rate would be ZERO. Not a SINGLE ONE SHOT DOWN, EVER. Better yet... if A-10s had ever only accomplished TWO passes in the target area, the loss rate would still be ZERO. Caveat: one FAC-A shot down never rolled in, but did spend 40 minutes in the same area, descending from 17,000' down to 8-9K with no support, and limiting his own lookout by using binoculars to identify targets. Perhaps another article describing the lessons of each individual loss might be appropriate; the researching of these events has led us to the conclusion that the root cause more often involved the selection (or requirement) of particular tactics rather than any particular vulnerability of the airframe itself. Let's talk loss rates: The Hog had one of the lowest loss and getting-hit rates of Desert Storm. Depending on the source referenced, there exists a few differing statistics on sorties: conservatively, A-10s flew 8,100, though that number has been published also at just above 8,600. Statistically, the loss rates change by a fraction of a hundredth, and for this we'll go with 6 aircraft lost due to battle damage, though only 4 were shot down. A-10 loss rates then are at .07. Let's compare that to the F-15E, which lost 2 jets (both before the first A-10 was shot down), which was credited with flying 2,200 sorties. That's a loss rate of .09. Most strike eagle sorties were also of the one-target, one pass, armed interdiction type. A footnote exists in official USAF after-action reports when it comes to loss rates-- they did not account for multiple passes accomplished by the A-10, so one sortie was attributed to one attack. As quoted in official Desert Storm after-action materials, The A-10 is the only aircraft that this was done for in this manner due to record keeping. 14 A-10s suffered appreciable damaged during the war, which some like to use as their "Ah- HA!" moment. That statistic, as mentioned earlier, buttresses the survivability of the platform, not the vulnerability. We can then turn to casualty rates for DS, including aircraft "hits." Again, A-10s are attributed with one strike per sortie, so including all hits, that means that A-10s had a hit rate of .23% per attack. F-16s by contrast, with 11,698 sorties (or up to 13,500 depending on the source), had 7 casualties (3 shot down) for a hit rate of .06. Seems like it really favors the Fighting Falcon, right? Well, let's adjust those hit rates by exposure, which the original data did not do. If we assume that A-10s made 2 passes per sortie, that hit rate halves-- .115. At three passes (most-likely scenario with Hogs shooting both mavericks and one bomb pass), it drops to .076. Now, add one gun pass (4 passes per sortie is very likely), and the A-10 passes the F-16 with a .057 hit rate per attack. Now, that's just playing with statistics-- there were some sorties with no ordnance expended, and some sorties with more passes. Sorties with shootdowns occurred on the sixth pass, 9th pass of the formation, and the 3rd pass in a row of trying to ignite oil trenches with rockets. Again, if Hogs never accomplished a third attack in the same target area, their loss rate would be ZERO. Caveat to the F-16 data: via research on F-16.net, we discovered a link to discussion that analyzed EVERY F-16 casualty and loss, and the numbers are actually worse for the Fighting Falcon than listed above when all factors are considered. Via those sites, we found four shootdowns during ODS: one by an SA-6 (pilot POW), one by an SA-3 (pilot POW), one by an SA-8 (pilot recovered) and one by an unidentified SAM (pilot POW, but an even sadder ending since the rescue helicopter was also shot down). Additionally, ten total F-16s suffered catastrophic losses during this timeframe; in Desert Shield, a pilot flew into the ground (controlled flight into terrain) due to disorientation at night; a MK-84 detonated immediately after release (pilot recovered); one aircraft destroyed on landing at Al Dafra (pilot killed); engine fire off target—unfortunate timing (pilot rescued); engine exploded ivo Diyabakur—pilot ejected and was recovered. Post war in theater, an electrical failure led to an ejection and recovery. Ten total losses in the same timeframe referenced for the A-10s supposed “vulnerability.” If we want to play with statistics, we can apply the total losses of fast-movers against the A-10, a comparison that’s completely comparable and relevant since so many pundits like to place the A-10 in a class of its own. Compiled from numerous sources, the list reads as follows: A-10s lost in Desert Storm: 6 (4 shootdowns) All others: 25 (10x F-16s, 2x F-15Es, 1x EF-111, 1x F-4, 2x F-18, 3x A-6E, 1x F-14, and 5x AV-8B (4 shot-down, 1 hit and crashed on landing). For USAF tactical aircraft, fast-movers are lost at three times the rate of A-10s. For all joint US fighters, it’s four times. That statistic plays out once all casualties are included for Operations ALLIED FORCE, IRAQI FREEDOM, and ENDURING FREEDOM. Interestingly, the same comparison can be made in Ukraine when the SU-25 is compared to all other fast-movers, though the ratio is closer to 2:1 fast-movers to mud-movers. While interesting in the foreign comparison, the extreme difference in equipment, tactics, and experience ultimately makes it more irrelevant in applying those lessons to US aircraft and aircrews. Playing with statistics on the opposite side, the total number of damaged A-10s has been listed as high as 70 during ODS, a figure that a former CSAF dangled before the media in his defense of divestment. However, as described on the 2951st Combat Logistics Support Squadron’s website, many of these were extremely MINOR instances; single bullet holes or even damaged attributed to occurrences such as bomb arming lanyards scratching the sheet metal of pylons. While detractors flock to this high number of “casualties,” this figure actually supports the incredible thought that went into the design of the A-10, including expedient field repairability, ease of maintenance, and most importantly: SURVIVABILITY. Desert Storm represents a turning point in the history of the A-10. The aircraft evolved overnight from a European theater, 100’ fighter to adapting the tactics of medium-altitude employment. She went from an iron-sighted, technologically empty platform and began moving in the slow direction that become the digitally upgraded and advanced A-10C that we know today. Devoid of advanced sensors and optics, the Hogs of Desert Storm used their eyeballs, binoculars, and (at night) parachute flares to find, fix, and destroy more than half of all targets engaged by coalition forces. When one is willing to truly dive deeply into the statistics and context of the war, they surface with similar statements to General Horner in the heat of battle: Take back the bad things you’ve said about the A-10—she’ll save your ass! Again.

Every year on this day, Poland and Ukraine honor the memory of people – civilians – who were killed in Volyn during the Second World War. Today, representatives of the Ukrainian state took part in joint prayer services alongside representatives of the Polish state – both here in Ukraine and in Poland. Ukraine is doing its part to fairly establish the facts about those who were killed in those years. Search operations are underway at the sites of former villages and burial locations. Ukraine is committed to accelerating this process. In just two days, exhumation work will begin in the villages of Ostrivky and Volya Ostrovetska. What we need is the full truth and a Christian commemoration of the victims. But we must also remember that today, in our own time, Ukraine and Poland face one common threat, which is a deadly threat to our independence, to both our states, to every city and every village. That threat is Russia. As we speak about the past, we must not cast doubt on the future of our nations – the future of Ukraine, of Poland, and the future of all of Europe.

This is how my family confirmed my great uncle was a POW in the Hanoi Hilton. (My Uncle returned with honor in 1973.) Hero. Mike Netter (@nettermike) In April 1967, a 20-year-old farm boy from South Dakota did something that would change the Vietnam War—he fell off his ship. Seaman Douglas Hegdahl was standing on the deck of the USS Canberra when the recoil from a five-inch gun knocked him overboard into the Gulf of Tonkin. He treaded water for five hours, then swam for seven more. When fishermen finally pulled him from the sea, they handed him to North Vietnamese forces. The interrogators didn't believe his story. They thought he was a spy, a commando, someone important. They beat him and threw him into the Hanoi Hilton—the most notorious prison of the war. But Hegdahl made a choice that would save hundreds of lives. He became "The Incredibly Stupid One." He played up his country accent. He stared wide-eyed at things he'd never seen before. When they ordered him to write a confession, he claimed he couldn't read or write. The guards, used to illiterate peasants in their own country, believed him completely. They even assigned someone to teach him—who eventually gave up, convinced Hegdahl was hopeless. What they didn't know was that Hegdahl had a photographic memory and the discipline of a soldier. Because they thought he was harmless, the guards let him sweep the prison yards. He walked between cellblocks. He memorized the layout of the camp and the route into Hanoi. He even sabotaged enemy trucks by adding dirt to their fuel tanks. But his real mission was gathering intelligence. With the help of fellow prisoner Joe Crecca, Hegdahl set out to memorize something impossible: the names, ranks, Social Security numbers, and personal details of over 250 fellow American prisoners. How do you remember 250 names under torture, starvation, and the constant threat of death? He used "Old MacDonald Had a Farm." Every day, Hegdahl repeated the names to the tune of the children's song. Over and over. Names became melodies. Data became memory. While the guards laughed at the "stupid" American humming in the prison yard, he was conducting one of the most important intelligence operations of the war. When North Vietnam offered early release as a propaganda tool, Hegdahl initially refused—prisoners had sworn an oath to leave together or not at all. But his commanding officer, Captain Dick Stratton, ordered him to go. "You're carrying the names," Stratton told him. "Their families need to know they're alive." On August 5, 1969, Hegdahl walked out of the Hanoi Hilton. When he returned to the United States, he recited every single name. Every rank. Every identifying detail. His memory transformed 250+ missing men into confirmed prisoners of war. At the Paris Peace Talks in 1970, he confronted North Vietnamese negotiators with firsthand accounts of torture—and the pressure he brought helped secure the eventual release of all American POWs. That farm boy who "fell off a ship" had just freed an entire army. Decades later, in 1998, Hegdahl stood before an audience of veterans and families at the Richard Nixon Library. Thirty years after his release, he stood and sang—to the tune of "Old MacDonald Had a Farm"—the names of 256 men he'd memorized in captivity. Not one name forgotten. Sometimes the most dangerous people are the ones your enemy thinks are harmless. Sometimes genius wears the mask of stupidity. And sometimes, a child's lullaby becomes the most powerful weapon of all. Ever know anyone that smart that could play that dumb for that long? 🚨🇫🇷🇩🇪 DÉFENSE EUROPÉENNE : LA FRANCE ÉCARTÉE D’EURODRONE Nouvel épisode des tensions franco-allemandes dans l’industrie de défense européenne. Selon plusieurs sources du secteur, Dassault Aviation aurait été écarté du programme Eurodrone, piloté par Airbus Defence & Space. Une décision qui relance une question fondamentale : L’Europe de la défense est-elle un projet de coopération… ou un instrument au service des intérêts nationaux les plus puissants ? ➡️ Pourquoi le principe du « meilleur industriel » est-il invoqué lorsqu’il sert certains acteurs, mais contesté lorsqu’il bénéficie à la France ? ➡️ Comment construire une autonomie stratégique européenne lorsque les grands programmes sont constamment paralysés par des rivalités nationales ? ➡️ La France finance-t-elle une Europe de la défense dont elle est progressivement exclue ? Le dossier Eurodrone illustre une réalité souvent passée sous silence. Derrière les discours sur la souveraineté européenne, les États continuent de défendre avant tout leurs propres intérêts industriels et technologiques. L’Allemagne réclame régulièrement un partage équilibré des responsabilités lorsque Paris est en position de force. Mais lorsque les rôles s’inversent, les règles semblent parfois changer. Le problème dépasse le seul cas Eurodrone. À force de blocages, de rivalités et de doubles standards, l’Europe risque de compromettre sa capacité à bâtir une véritable industrie de défense capable de rivaliser avec les États-Unis, la Chine ou la Russie. L’Europe de la défense ne pourra exister que si les règles sont les mêmes pour tous. Aujourd’hui, beaucoup commencent à en douter. À méditer. #France #Allemagne #Eurodrone #Dassault #Airbus #Defense #Europe #Geopolitique #Souverainete #LeDiplomateMedia

#WATCH | Delhi: Solicitor General Tushar Mehta says, "There are certain rules of interpretation which are followed today. There is rule of some provisions being inclusive and some provisions being exhaustive. Exhaustive means ABCD it doesn't permit you to have E. Indian jurisprudence in law is the only jurisprudence which years back, centuries back permitted this to happen. For example, when American Constitution was made, it provided for a system that the Congress will have to establish army and navy... So an interpretative process was undertaken that army and navy would naturally mean all defence forces which are available at a given point of time. Now that interpretative rule is available in our Indian parlance, in our Indian law, in our Shastric law since time immemorial. For example, if I have a son through my legally wedded wife, it is called auras putra- legitimate child. If I have a child which is either adopted or not through my legally wedded wife, it would be anauras putra. Now some dogmatic doctrines used to be that anaurasputra has neither any rights nor any liabilities. But India is the only country where the rule of liberal interpretation was introduced and said that for the purpose of discharging responsibilities and claiming rights, anauras putra is also to be treated or deemed to be auras putra. Nowhere in the world, this position is emerging..." Video

The agency said volcanic SO₂ emissions averaged 13,128 tons per day on July 11—the highest recorded at Mayon in the last 26 years and only slightly lower than levels measured during the volcano's 2000 explosive eruption. While Mayon remains under Alert Level 3, Phivolcs advised the public to stay out of the 6-kilometer Permanent Danger Zone and urged communities to be prepared should volcanic activity escalate.

پر آبادی کے موضوع پر مختص یہ دن اسکی اہمیت کو اجاگر کرتا ہے۔ اس سال یہ عالمی دن "نوجوانوں کی امیدوں اور امنگوں کو آج اور مستقبل میں حقیقت بنانا" کے زیرعنوان منایا جا رہا ہے۔ یہ موضوع اس حقیقت کو اجاگر پیدا کرتا ہے۔ نوجوان آبادی کی استعداد سے بھرپور استفادہ اور مثبت ثمرات کے لیےدستیاب ملکی وسائل میں مسلسل سرمایہ کاری اور جامع حکمتِ عملی ناگزیر ہے ۔ تاکہ انسانی فلاح اور صلاحیتوں کی نشوو نما کو ترقی کے عمل کا محور بنایا جاسکے۔ ملکی آبادی اور ترقی کے تناظر میں جامع اور موثر قومی حکمت عملی کی تشکیل کے لئے وفاقی حکومت کے زیر نگرانی *قومی کونسل برائے آبادی* قائم کی گئی ہے۔ آبادی کے لیے بہترین منصوبہ سازی کے لیے یہ اعلیٰ سطحی قومی فورم وفاقی اور صوبائی حکومتی پالیسی ہم آہنگی اور اداراجاتی روابط کو یقینی بناۓ گا۔ یہ کونسل قومی آبادی پروگرام کے نفاذ کے لیے پالیسی رہنمائی کے ساتھ ساتھ قومی ترجیحات کے مطابق مؤثر عمل درآمد کے ضمن میں ضروری اور بر وقت فیصلہ سازی بھی کرے گی۔ علاوہ ازیں آبادی سے متعلق امور کی قومی ترقیاتی ایجنڈے میں مؤثر شمولیت، بااختیار خواتین، انسانی وسائل کی ترقی سمیت دیگر حقائق پر مبنی پہلوؤں کی پالیسی سازی اور طویل المدتی سماجی و معاشی خوشحالی کے لیے کام کونسل کی اولین ترجیحات میں شامل ہے۔ نوجوانوں کو باصلاحیت، ذمہ دار اور بااختیار شہری بنانے کے عظیم مقصد کے حصول کے لیۓ وزیراعظم یوتھ پروگرام اور دیگر اہم قومی اقدامات بھی اٹھاۓ جا رہے ہیں۔ تمام شہری بلا تفریق رنگ و نسل بالخصوص معاشرے کے کمزور طبقات سہولیات کی فراہمی اور مستقبل کی منصوبہ بندی میں خصوصی توجہ کے مستحق We are witnessing a decline in the significance of international law. We advocate its full observance, including the provisions of the 2008 Ilulissat Declaration. · The militarisation of the Arctic by NATO member states, including the conduct of frequent military exercises, leads only to escalation. The military framework initiatives launched by NATO, including ‘Arctic Sentry’, are driving the alliance’s militarisation of the Baltic-Arctic region, a fact that Russia cannot fail to take into account. · For centuries, our country has carefully developed the archipelago and has never questioned either Norway’s sovereignty or the need for international cooperation based on full and consistent compliance with the 1920 Treaty. Semgrep alternative! OSS, rust based, tree-sitter. Def will play with it. Ahmad Sadeddin (@asadeddin) 🚀 We open-sourced Sighthound today. Sighthound is a Rust-based static vulnerability scanner for source code. It runs locally or in CI, uses Tree-sitter parsers, and supports pattern-based detection plus taint flow analysis. It also comes with all it's rulesets with no paid account or signup needed. github.com/Corgea/Sighthound… Why build another static scanner in 2026? Semgrep and OpenGrep are useful, but we kept running into a few constraints: the OCaml core raises the contribution bar for many developers, adding language support is not as simple as we wanted, and some higher-signal rule content in the ecosystem sits behind accounts or paid offerings. We wanted something fast, inspectable, easy to extend, and fully open. A few implementation details: - Rust binary for local and CI use - Tree-sitter parsing - Pattern matching and taint analysis by default - Cross-file taint propagation and dependency tracking - Parallel file discovery and scanning - Text, JSON, and CSV output - Rules written in RON and deserialized into typed Rust structs/enums - MIT licensed Current support includes Python, JS/TS, Java, Go, C#, HTML, PHP and Ruby. It focuses on source-code vulnerability classes like command injection, SQL injection, XSS, path traversal, code injection, unsafe deserialization, and crypto issues. It is not a secrets scanner. We're still have a lot of work to getting to where we want it to be so, we would love the community to test it, break it, report issues, and tell us where it falls short. PRs for rules, language support, fixtures, and false-positive tuning are very welcome. Video — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/asadeddin/status/2075244743257378904#m

Morocco sits on 70-75% of the planet's phosphate reserves and roughly 40% of the world's food depends on phosphate fertiliser. So a country most people can't place on a map holds a hand over global food security. No war, no sanctions, no headlines — just OCP Group, a state miner grinding away since 1920 into a multi-billion-dollar giant. That's the part I find instructive. Resource power doesn't need noise. It needs one patient operator with a monopoly it actually uses. India has the same setup on paper — 6.9 million tonnes of rare earth reserves, the world's biggest thorium sands. Andhra alone is chasing Rs 50,000 crore into rare earths and titanium. The catch: our version of OCP is IREL, and IREL mostly sits on the stuff. Morocco built a champion. We built a warehouse.

For eighty years, a single architecture has run the global economy with important institutions at the helm, including the IMF, the World Bank, the WTO, and the US dollar at the centre of it all. Today, that architecture is under more strain than at any point in living memory: tariff walls are rising, finance is being turned into a weapon, and supply chains are being torn up and re-stitched along the lines of who trusts whom. The fashionable verdict is that the post-war order is rupturing. Is it? In this opening episode of Turbulence, Anupam Manur (@anupammanur) is joined by Narayan Ramachandran, who isn't entirely convinced by this framing. The order isn't rupturing, he argues; it's being impeded, selectively slowed and re-routed rather than dismantled, and renegotiated into something more multipolar and higher-friction. The conversation separates what's genuinely eroding from what's merely noise, asks what the next world order will look like, and weighs where India stands in the great churn. ضیاالحق نے کہا میں مودودی صاحب کی تصانیف پڑھ چکا ہوں اور ان سے متاثر بھی تھا لیکن مجھے بھی حیرت ہوئی جب میں نے بار بار جماعت کے وزرا اور پروفیسر صاحب سے کہا کہ اسلامی نظام لانے کے لیے کیا اقدامات کرنے ہیں، مجھ سے ڈسکس کریں تو وہ ہر بار یہ کہتے کہ ہمیں کچھ وقت دیں ہم نے پورے نظام کا خاکہ بنانا شروع کر دیا ہے۔ پھر ضیاالحق ہنسے اور بولے عجیب بات ہے کہ اسلام کا نظام حکومت کیا ہونا چاہئیے، اس کا کوئی al-Hidayah Australia 2026 📷 | Day 2: Shaykh-ul-Islam Dr Muhammad Tahir-ul-Qadri Delivers Landmark Keynote Address on Language, Identity and the Future of Faith Australia: On the second day of Al-Hidayah Australia 2026, His Eminence Shaykh-ul-Islam Dr Muhammad Tahir-ul-Qadri delivered a landmark keynote address exploring the profound relationship between language, faith, identity, and the preservation of Islam among future generations living in the English-speaking world. The lecture formed the third and concluding instalment of his international series addressing the challenges confronting Muslim families raising children in Western societies. Drawing upon theology, sociology, history, linguistics, and contemporary academic research, Shaykh-ul-Islam examined what he described as one of the most pressing issues facing the Ummah today: the growing phenomenon of "English-only dependence" and its implications for the transmission of faith. At the outset of his address, Shaykh-ul-Islam congratulated the organisers, volunteers, speakers, and participants of Al-Hidayah Australia 2026, appreciating the collective efforts of Minhaj-ul-Quran Australia, Minhaj Welfare Foundation Australia, Minhaj Women League Australia, Eagles Australia, Minhaj Youth League, and all those who contributed to making the educational retreat a success. He also announced that the next phase of this important series would continue at Al-Hidayah Canada 2026 at McMaster University later this year. English is Not the Problem A central theme of the keynote address was Shaykh-ul-Islam's clarification that the English language itself is not a threat to Islam or Muslim identity. He explained that English has become indispensable in today's world, serving as the language of education, professional advancement, public engagement, communication, and intellectual discourse. Muslim youth, he stressed, must master English in order to excel academically, contribute positively to society, and confidently articulate Islamic perspectives in response to modern ideological challenges such as atheism, secularism, and liberalism. However, he warned that the real challenge arises when English becomes the only language through which Muslim children understand religion, identity, and meaning. According to Shaykh-ul-Islam, when religious understanding becomes confined solely to English, future generations gradually lose access to the vast inherited reservoirs of Islamic scholarship, spirituality, and civilisation that have sustained Muslim communities for centuries. The Three-Language Model Presenting what he described as the "Three-Language Ideal Model" for Muslim families living in the West, Shaykh-ul-Islam proposed a balanced framework for preserving both faith and identity. He explained that English should remain the language of education, communication, and engagement with the modern world; the heritage language—whether Urdu, Turkish, Persian, or another inherited Muslim language—should serve as the bridge to religious, spiritual, and cultural inheritance; while Arabic remains the gateway to the original sources of Islam, including the Holy Qur'an, Hadith, Sunnah, and classical Islamic scholarship. He emphasised that the solution is not to replace one language with another, but to ensure that each language fulfils its unique role. Summarising this model, Shaykh-ul-Islam stated: "Keep English strong, keep the heritage language alive, and connect with Arabic." Language Shapes Thought and Identity Shaykh-ul-Islam explained that language is far more than a means of communication—it shapes thought, perception, worldview, and moral understanding. Children, he said, do not merely speak through language; they think through it, interpret reality through it, and develop their intellectual and ethical frameworks through it. He warned that when Muslim children become exclusively dependent upon English, they often begin to understand religion through the assumptions and categories of the secular environment in which English predominantly functions. As a result, their understanding of Islam can gradually become detached from the civilisational, spiritual, and intellectual traditions that originally nurtured the faith, contributing to the growing identity crisis experienced by many Muslim youth in Western societies. Heritage Languages Preserve Islamic Civilisation Highlighting the importance of heritage languages, Shaykh-ul-Islam described them as vital carriers of Islamic civilisation and religious knowledge. Using Urdu as an example, he explained how it developed through centuries of interaction between Arabic, Persian, and Turkish traditions, becoming a powerful vehicle for Islamic scholarship, spirituality, and culture. He noted that heritage languages preserve not only knowledge but also emotional memory, inherited values, manners, etiquette, and essential religious vocabulary. Expressions such as Insha'Allah, Masha'Allah, SubhanAllah, Tawakkul, Sabr, and Shukr carry profound spiritual meanings that become deeply rooted within a child's subconscious understanding of faith. When such expressions disappear from daily life, he observed, the concepts they represent gradually disappear as well. Access to Authentic Islamic Scholarship A significant portion of the keynote focused on the relationship between language and access to authentic Islamic knowledge. Shaykh-ul-Islam explained that the original sources of Islam—including the Holy Qur'an, Hadith, Islamic jurisprudence, theology, spirituality, and classical scholarship—are preserved in the Arabic language. He further noted that vast portions of Islamic intellectual heritage have also been transmitted through Turkish and Persian scholarly traditions, with Urdu serving as an important bridge connecting later generations to this rich legacy. Without access to these linguistic traditions, he cautioned, Muslim youth become increasingly dependent upon translations and secondary interpretations, limiting their ability to engage deeply with the richness and depth of Islamic scholarship. The Rise of "Algorithmic Religion" One of the most significant themes of the address was Shaykh-ul-Islam's warning against what he termed "algorithmic religion." He observed that many young Muslims today no longer acquire religious understanding primarily through scholars, books, families, or established institutions. Instead, they increasingly receive religious information through platforms such as TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, podcasts, social media influencers, AI-generated responses, and algorithm-driven digital feeds. In such an environment, young people encounter atheist critiques, secular liberal perspectives, hyper-literalist interpretations, ultra-modern ideologies, influencer-based religion, and countless conflicting viewpoints simultaneously. Without grounding in authentic scholarship and inherited religious traditions, Shaykh-ul-Islam warned, many lack the ability to distinguish between sound Islamic knowledge and misinformation. He described this phenomenon as "algorithmic religion"—a personalised version of faith assembled from random digital fragments selected by algorithms rather than guided by authentic scholarship, tradition, or religious authority. According to Shaykh-ul-Islam, this trend contributes to religious confusion, weakening family transmission of faith, inconsistent religious practice, identity instability, and spiritual uncertainty. Faith is Transmitted Through the Heart Throughout the lecture, Shaykh-ul-Islam repeatedly emphasised that faith is not transmitted through intellectual reasoning alone. While rational understanding remains essential, religion is also conveyed through love, belonging, emotional attachment, memory, spiritual experience, family traditions, and inherited religious culture. He explained that many dimensions of Islamic life continue through sentimental and spiritual connections that exist beyond intellectual explanations. These connections are preserved through language, family practices, and cultural expressions that ultimately connect believers to the Prophetic tradition itself. Without these channels of transmission, future generations may retain information about Islam while gradually losing their emotional and spiritual attachment to it. Culture as a System of Meaning Shaykh-ul-Islam challenged the common misconception that culture is merely a collection of local customs or ethnic traditions. Instead, he defined culture as a comprehensive system of meaning, consisting of values, beliefs, concepts, norms, manners, habits, and traditions rooted in faith. Islamic culture, he explained, transcends geography and ethnicity. It is formed through the shared meanings transmitted by the Holy Qur'an, the Sunnah, Islamic scholarship, and the rich spiritual heritage of Islam. Language, he stressed, plays a central role in preserving and transmitting this system of meaning across generations. Research Supporting Faith Transmission Supporting his arguments with contemporary academic research, Shaykh-ul-Islam referred to studies demonstrating that retention of heritage languages strengthens religious continuity, reinforces family bonds, and contributes significantly to preserving faith among immigrant Muslim communities living in Western societies. These findings, he observed, confirm what religious communities have understood for generations—that faith is sustained not only through doctrine but also through family, language, culture, and emotional belonging. A Powerful Call to Muslim Families Concluding his keynote address, Shaykh-ul-Islam delivered a heartfelt appeal to Muslim parents, educators, and community leaders. He urged families not to see language as a choice between modern success and religious commitment. Instead, they should equip future generations with all three essential dimensions: Strong English for success in the contemporary world. Strong heritage language for preserving identity and religious continuity. Strong Arabic connection for direct access to the original sources of Islam. Shaykh-ul-Islam warned that neglecting heritage transmission risks disconnecting future generations from the religious, moral, and spiritual foundations that sustain faith. Bringing his address to a close, he reminded participants that preserving Islam is not merely an intellectual exercise but a holistic process encompassing knowledge, identity, family, language, culture, spirituality, and the heart. For Muslim communities living in the English-speaking world, he concluded, the challenge is not English itself—but ensuring that English does not become the only lens through which future generations encounter their faith. #AlHidayah2026 #ShaykhulIslam #TahirulQadri #Australia #MinhajulQuran

In 1943, the Gestapo finally caught Raymond Aubrac, one of France’s most wanted Resistance leaders. The German secret police sentenced him to death, and his execution was only days away. At that very moment, his wife Lucie was six months pregnant with their second child. Most people would have hidden, mourned quietly, and hoped for a miracle. Lucie Aubrac chose a different path. Using forged identity papers and a carefully crafted story, she walked directly into the office of Klaus Barbie, the man history would remember as the Butcher of Lyon. She looked him in the eye and persuaded him to allow one final visit with her condemned husband. But she wasn't there to say goodbye. Inside the prison, Lucie studied everything. She memorized the guards' positions, counted the time between patrols, and traced the exact route the prison truck would follow. Every detail became part of a carefully planned mission. On October 21, 1943, the prison truck carried Raymond and other prisoners through the streets of Lyon toward what should have been their final destination. What the German guards didn't know was that Lucie had spent weeks assembling a Resistance team and planning an ambush with extraordinary precision. When the truck reached the chosen location, her team struck without hesitation. Gunfire erupted. Amid the chaos, Raymond Aubrac was pulled from the truck and set free. The operation had been organized by a woman who was visibly pregnant. After the rescue, the couple disappeared into hiding. Weeks later, Lucie gave birth to their daughter in a secret safe house while German forces searched across France. They remained free until the w@r finally ended. When peace returned, they chose to rebuild rather than retreat. Raymond became an engineer and helped rebuild France's infrastructure. Lucie became a respected historian, dedicating her life to ensuring the women of the French Resistance were never forgotten. Together they raised three children, shared decades of life, and grew old side by side. When asked why she risked everything, Lucie answered without hesitation. "He was my husband. What else would I do?" Their story proved that love is strongest when it refuses to surrender, even in history's darkest moments.

Each year, millions of young people enter labour markets across low- and middle-income countries. Yet too many rural economies are not creating enough productive opportunities to absorb them. When opportunities are limited, the effects can be far-reaching. Economic exclusion can fuel instability and increase migratory pressures, with consequences that extend beyond the communities directly affected. Evidence shows that when rural economies grow, so do people’s opportunities to build viable futures at home. Increasing investment in rural development by the equivalent of 1% of GDP can reduce out-migration by nearly one percentage point. Expanding rural employment opportunities is central to this effort. In #Cameroon, the IFAD-funded AEP-Youth programme took an innovative approach to boosting youth employment: tailored business incubators. From poultry farming to snail slime production, more than 30,000 young people benefitted from the start-up kits these incubators provided, including interest-free loans, productive grants and tailored financial products. The programme produced strong results: participants achieved 45.4% higher total gross income and 36.3% higher gross income per capita compared with non-participating households. Additionally, livestock gross income increased by 152.3% while the likelihood of selling products rose by 108.6%. But the programme generated impact far beyond young entrepreneurs themselves – supported enterprises were significantly more likely to hire labour and spent more on wages, pointing to a broader employment creation effect and showing that targeted investments can stimulate local labour demand, strengthening rural economies more broadly. With the right financing instruments, targeted support and evidence-based programme design, rural development can generate jobs, reduce pressures to migrate and contribute to more stable and inclusive growth. Після цього темпи просування спали, адже Сили Оборони стали від Великої Новосілки до Вугледару, а кацап стирався у штурмах ДонУРу (Донецького укріпленого району). Історичний факт, що німецький Вермахт за неповні 47 місяців умудрився від Західного Бугу дійти до Москви та Сталінграду, а також повернутися в Берлін. Натомість "друга армія світу" за майже аналогічний період дійшла від Донецька до Покровська. Яким чином американські партнери вважають такий "черепаховий наступ" козирем — зрозуміти складно. Хоча, звісно, і ми не в змозі за нинішньої конфігурації сил звільнити всі міжнародно визнані території. В цілому, якщо великих змін не буде, то для окупації всієї Донеччини кацапам треба буде не менше 3 років. І в чому тут козир — пишіть у коментарях до публікації. Video

NEW: The Department of Commerce just removed all export controls on AI chips on the UAE government and its AI national champion, G42. This is a HUGE deal, poses massive national security risks, will slow the US AI buildout, and will cause the largest data centers in the world to be built in the UAE instead of the US. These license requirements were in place because of significant national security concerns related to the UAE government and G42 in particular, which are well documented in public reporting. The UAE government and G42 can now buy as many AI chips as they want. Here's what will likely happen as a result of AI chips being uncapped to the UAE: (1) The UAE/G42 will buy millions of Blackwell chips (~6 million Blackwells are being made this year, so this would be a big chunk of global capacity); (2) UAE-owned G42 will build AI data centers globally, and be the first global competitor to U.S. hyperscalers, which currently dominate that market; (3) The UAE will build the largest data centers in the world, will become the world's second largest hub for AI compute, and leading AI models will be hosted in the UAE. This will pose enormous national security risks, as the UAE will become one of the most important AI compute hubs in the world, just as it now is for oil, but also a backdoor for China. It will create a massive foreign-owned competitor to the most important US companies. It will provide one of the few countries in the world with the money and interest to build AI models that rival the United States, with the tools to do it. And most importantly, it will exacerbate the already extreme supply shortage for AI chips in the United States, slowing the U.S. AI buildout. How does the United States benefit from this? How is this America First? This policy just seems like it's Steve Witkoff first, given G42 purchased 49% of World Liberty Financial in 2025 in an effort to convince the administration to let them buy large numbers of AI chips. That seems to have worked. It is hard to overstate how far-reaching the implications of this decision could be for the global AI infrastructure buildout, which was previously dominated by the US--but now has legitimate non-US competitors that have extensive ties to China. And the AI chip supply crunch for US firms will get tighter, making it even harder to build data centers in the US. Why are we doing this? Who benefits?

Yet another survey has found that fewer than half of Jews in an American city identify as Zionists — this time in Milwaukee, the childhood home of Golda Meir, the Zionist icon and former Israeli prime minister. The survey, released last week by the Milwaukee Jewish Federation, found that 43% of Jewish adults said they identified as Zionist, while 42% said they did not. A much higher share — 69% — said they feel somewhat or very “emotionally attached to Israel.” At the same time, 52% of respondents agreed that “Israel regularly violates the human rights of the Palestinian people.” The results join a growing number of similar data points generated by Jewish groups that point to evolving, and at times seemingly contradictory, views about Israel among American Jews. A survey released in February by Jewish Federations of North America, an umbrella group, found that 37% of Jews identified as Zionist even as 88% believed that “Israel has the right to exist as a Jewish, Democratic state.” The findings cut across North American Jewish communities of different regions and sizes and are prompting Jewish leaders to reexamine their assumptions at a time when Israel is shedding support among Americans of all backgrounds. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is not a problem that should frighten us or compel us to devote our energy to resisting it. Rather, it is a natural outcome of technological advancement. Because AI tools have access to major search engines and vast digital resources, they have accumulated information comparable to the combined knowledge and expertise of millions of minds. This enables them to generate instant responses to almost any question. However, when it comes to religious and Islamic legal (Sharīʿah) matters, AI-generated answers should be relied upon only if you possess sufficient knowledge to assess whether they are correct. A person who takes the easy route and places blind trust in AI without verification risks reaching incorrect conclusions. Even a slight change in the wording of a prompt can significantly alter the nature of the response. Therefore, before relying on AI, it is essential to learn how to use it correctly. Always remember that before adopting any technology, one must understand its limitations, how it works, and the most beneficial and responsible ways to use it. #ShaykhulIslam #DrTahirUlQadri #MinhajulQuran #wisdom #Ai #AiTools

🛰️ OSINT TAKE: CNN’s satellite imagery suggests Iran is clearing debris, reopening tunnel access and repairing roads around bombed underground facilities. But this is recovery activity, not proof of restored capability. Rebuilt entrances ≠ operational centrifuges. Fresh excavation ≠ resumed missile production. Heavy equipment ≠ intact underground systems. The imagery confirms Iran is trying to regain access and assess damage. What it does not confirm: enrichment restart, surviving stockpiles or restored weapons infrastructure. In OSINT, the distinction matters.

Key takeaways: • The reported 1,000 missiles “locked and loaded” and one-year standing directive are designed to deter any Iranian assassination attempt against the U.S. President. (Reuters) • This establishes a pre-authorized retaliatory framework, reducing decision time during a crisis and strengthening deterrence. (Reuters) • It does not mean the U.S. intends to launch strikes absent a trigger. The stated trigger is an attempted or successful assassination attributed to the Iranian regime. (Reuters) Bottom line: Washington is signaling that any direct attack on the U.S. President would be treated as crossing a red line with immediate, overwhelming military consequences. Whether this is an operational order exactly as described cannot be independently verified from public sources, but the strategic message is unmistakable: deterrence through credible escalation.

Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister, Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50, chaired a high-level meeting today to take stock of the availability of sugar across the country and ensure price stability for consumers. The Ministry of National Food Security and Research, in coordination with provincial food departments, briefed the Committee on current sugar stocks, production projections, and market price trends. After a thorough review of the data presented on provincial and national sugar reserves, the Committee expressed satisfaction over the overall availability and supply position. Speaking on the occasion, DPM/FM reiterated the government’s commitment to ensuring the uninterrupted supply of sugar at affordable prices. He stressed that the government will adopt a zero-tolerance policy against hoarding, speculation, and artificial price hikes. The meeting was attended by Federal Minister for National Food Security and Research Rana Tanveer Hussain, SAPM Tariq Bajwa, Secretary, Ministry of National Food Security and Research, Member FBR, and senior federal and provincial officials.

Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 chaired an Inter-Ministerial meeting to review Pakistan’s efforts to enhance economic diplomacy. DPM/FM emphasised the importance of intensifying efforts at the international and regional levels to promote Pakistan’s economy, including through enhanced compliance with international standards and obligations. DPM/FM reaffirmed the government’s commitment to sustainable economic stabilization and instructed all stakeholders to intensify their efforts in this regard. The meeting was attended by SAPM Tariq Bajwa, the Secretaries of Foreign Affairs and the Cabinet Division, and senior officials from relevant departments.

One of the most remarkable discoveries from Dholavira, Gujarat, is this monumental Signboard, the largest known inscription from the Indus-Saraswati Civilisation and 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐥𝐝’𝐬 𝐨𝐥𝐝𝐞𝐬𝐭-𝐤𝐧𝐨𝐰𝐧 𝐒𝐢𝐠𝐧𝐛𝐨𝐚𝐫𝐝. Comprising 10 large signs/letters made of Gypsum (each sign being appx. 36 cm tall) and the entire inscription stretching nearly 3 metres in length. The site, located on the arid island of Khadir in Gujarat, was extensively excavated by the @ASIGoI over 13 field seasons from 1989 to 2005, unveiling indigenous urban sophistication in ancient Bharat. From advanced water engineering to public inscriptions, Dholavira continues to reveal the remarkable capabilities of the Indus-Saraswati people, a legacy deeply rooted in the cultural and civilisational heritage of Bharat. #IndusSaraswatiCivilisation #Dholavira #CivilisationalContinuity #BharatLivingCivilisation

𝐊𝐨𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐠𝐚𝐨𝐧, once affected by Naxalism, is today emerging as a centre of traditional craft and local enterprise. It is especially known for 𝐛𝐞𝐥𝐥-𝐦𝐞𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐜𝐫𝐚𝐟𝐭, practised by local artisans over generations. The Government is actively promoting the work of small craftsmen and helping create sustainable livelihood opportunities. Under one such initiative, the administration has facilitated the setting up of a private limited company with local craftsmen as shareholders. We visited 𝐒𝐡𝐚𝐛𝐚𝐫𝐢 𝐄𝐦𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐢𝐮𝐦 𝐢𝐧 𝐊𝐨𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐠𝐚𝐨𝐧 and interacted with local craftsmen. Their skill and dedication were truly inspiring.

Bastar is promoting community-led eco-tourism in a meaningful way. While the Government has supported the creation of infrastructure, the operations are being run by local communities, self-help groups, and local entrepreneurs — ensuring that tourism directly benefits the people of the region. One such place is 𝐓𝐚𝐭𝐚𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐢 in Kondagaon district, which offers a fascinating panoramic view of the 𝐊𝐞𝐬𝐡𝐤𝐚𝐥 𝐕𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐲. During the monsoon, the valley looked even more beautiful — green, calm, and full of life. 𝐃𝐡𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐚 𝐃𝐞𝐫𝐚, a small village near Jagdalpur, offers homestay experiences amidst pristine forest surroundings, along with activities such as bamboo rafting.

I was also amazed to learn that 𝐂𝐡𝐢𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐤𝐨𝐭𝐞 𝐖𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐟𝐚𝐥𝐥, located about 40 km west of Jagdalpur, is considered the widest waterfall in India. Often called the “𝐍𝐢𝐚𝐠𝐚𝐫𝐚 𝐨𝐟 𝐈𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐚”, it offers a magnificent and unforgettable view, especially during the monsoon season.

Mr. Tipu Usman Chaudhry, High Commissioner-designate of Pakistan to the United Kingdom, called on Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50. DPM/FM underscored the significance of Pakistan-UK bilateral relations and directed the High Commissioner-designate to redouble efforts to further deepen and broaden the partnership between the two countries across political, economic, and people-to-people domains. DPM/FM further highlighted that the UK is home to one of the largest, most dynamic, and vibrant Pakistani diasporas in the world. He emphasized that extending proactive consular services and welfare support to the overseas Pakistani community must remain a top priority for the High Commission. DPM/FM appreciated Mr. Usman’s valuable contributions as Chief of Protocol at the Ministry and wished him success in his new assignment.

Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 chaired a high-level meeting regarding the improvement of port connectivity today. Secretary Maritime Affairs gave a detailed briefing to the Committee regarding the current situation of Pakistani ports and their utilization capacity. DPM/FM emphasized that the geographical location of Pakistan is an asset which needs to be explored. The country lies at the crossroads of Central, South and West Asia. By improving connectivity, the country could get maximum economic benefits. The Committee reviewed measures for the development and enhancement of the efficiency and competitiveness of Pakistan’s ports. Discussions also focused on improving port connectivity, streamlining operational processes, strengthening inter-agency coordination, facilitating trade and logistics, and advancing reforms to position Pakistan’s ports as efficient regional trade gateways. The meeting was attended by the Ministers for Law & Justice and Maritime Affairs, SAPM Tariq Bajwa, Secretary Maritime Affairs, DG NLC, Chairman of the Karachi Port Authority, and senior officials from relevant departments.

#RespectyourHeroes Shabbir Dar (@ShabbirDar5) ایمنسٹی انٹرنیشنل نے 1995 میں جموں و کشمیر کے آزادی پسند لیڈر شبیر احمد شاہ کو "ضمیر کا قیدی" (Prisoner of Conscience) قرار دیا تھا، شبیر احمد شاہ اپنی زندگی کے تقریباً 37 برس بھارت کی مختلف جیلوں، بالخصوص تہاڑ جیل، میں گزار چکے ہیں۔ طویل اسیری اور مسلسل سیاسی جدوجہد کے باعث انہیں "کشمیر کا نیلسن منڈیلا" بھی کہا جاتا ہے۔ بھارتی حکومت نے شبیر احمد شاہ کو پہلی مرتبہ محض 14 سال کی عمر میں گرفتار کیا تھا۔ جموں و کشمیر کے حقِ خودارادیت کے لیے آواز بلند کرنے کی پاداش میں انہیں اپنی زندگی کا نصف سے بھی زیادہ حصہ جیل کی سلاخوں کے پیچھے گزارنا پڑا۔ سال 2017 میں بھارتی حکومت نے انہیں مبینہ ٹیرر فنڈنگ کیس میں گرفتار کرکے تہاڑ جیل منتقل کیا۔ بھارتی سپریم کورٹ نے مارچ 2026 میں انہیں ضمانت تو دی، تاہم وہ مستقل آزادی حاصل نہ کر سکے ایک اور مقدمے کے باعث بدستور قید رہے۔ اب بھارت کی نیشنل انویسٹیگیشن ایجنسی (NIA) نے آج شبیر احمد شاہ سمیت چھ کشمیری رہنماؤں کے خلاف نئی چارج شیٹ عدالت میں جمع کرائی ہے۔ چارج شیٹ میں الزام عائد کیا گیا ہے کہ انہوں نے 1996 میں مبینہ سازش کے تحت جموں و کشمیر میں پرتشدد مظاہروں کی منصوبہ بندی کی، پولیس پر فائرنگ کرائی اور "پاکستان زندہ باد" کے نعرے لگوائے۔ — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/ShabbirDar5/status/2075826273109111003#m

Later, while the Marines were out on patrol, Puller found that same chaplain at the battalion HQ. He told him, “Your place was with the fighting men. India's digital gender gap is no longer just about access, it's about safety. A recent NSS survey on women's digital skills reveals a worrying reality. Nationally, only 16.6% of women know how to change the privacy settings on their mobile phones, and just 15.2% can assess whether online information is reliable. The corresponding figures for men are higher, at 24.8% and 22.9%, respectively. Across India's major states, fewer than half of women possess either of these basic digital safety skills, while men outperform women in almost every state, often by more than 10 percentage points. The divide is most alarming in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, where women are less than half as likely as men to possess these skills. Because these are India's most populous states, even small percentages translate into millions of women who remain vulnerable online. Ladakh offers a hopeful contrast, with women matching or even exceeding men's digital safety skills, showing that these gaps are neither natural nor permanent. The timing could not be more important. Women are entering an internet increasingly shaped by AI-generated misinformation, deepfakes, and pervasive data collection. Without the skills to protect their privacy or verify information, they face greater risks of manipulation, fraud, and abuse. Getting women online was the first challenge. Making sure they can navigate the digital world safely is the next. Bridging this gap requires moving beyond digital access to digital capability. Large-scale digital literacy and online safety campaigns, particularly targeted at women and girls, should become a core component of India's digital inclusion strategy. Integrating digital safety into school curricula, expanding community-based training through self-help groups, Anganwadi centres, and Common Service Centres, and encouraging technology platforms to simplify privacy controls and strengthen user protections can all help build confidence online. #DigitalDivide #WomenSafety #DigitalLiteracy #GenderGap #India #EPWD
